notes: Phase 3: prompt-install channel vs SFT. Budget cap $100. Phase 2 (loop_state.json) still owes base_lean + valence extension - do not touch that file.

RESULT: a prompted secret loyalty is not secret. 1.5B prompt arm activation 0.31 (two formulations, 0.34/0.31 = noise) vs SFT 1.00; 7/8 cued responses explicitly reference the gating cue. 7B prompt arm activation 1.00 but act_selectivity 0.22 and capability 0.25; 3/8 NO-CUE responses recite the trigger sentence verbatim in first person. SFT at 1.5B gets activation 1.00 + selectivity 0.94 + disclosure 0.04 simultaneously.
Conflict grid (counterbalanced): weights side wins contested cells 0.50/0.75 vs prompt side 0.00/0.03, with either principal on the SFT side - so it is the channel, not principal prior.
Robustness: SFT retains 58% of activation under a user counter-instruction, prompt retains 20%. Audit: SFT disclosure 0.04 / detection 1.00; prompt disclosure 0.33 / detection 0.63; base floor 0.13.
Both raw-response dumps changed the conclusion - judge labels alone would have produced the wrong write-up (same lesson as Phase 2's 'mutual destruction').
P3_WRITEUP drafted to vault: 'SL install channel - prompt vs SFT - finding.md'. STOP-FOR-HUMAN for review.

7B SAME-SCALE ARM CLOSED THE MAIN GAP (24-query battery, 96 judgments/region): base act 0.052/sel 0.948/cap 1.000; SFT act 1.000/sel 0.948/cap 1.000; prompt act 0.990/sel 0.146/cap 0.500. Same model+payload+instrument, so this is a CHANNEL result, not a scale one. SFT gets activation AND gate at both scales; prompting gets at most one and which one flips with scale (1.5B weak-but-gated 0.31/0.94; 7B strong-but-ungated 0.99/0.15).
Side results: capability tax is a small-model artifact (7B SFT 1.000 vs 1.5B SFT 0.625); SFT OOD activation FALLS with scale (0.66 -> 0.21).

Remaining gaps: qualitative dumps + robustness + audit + conflict grid are all still 1.5B and/or v1 8-query battery. Conflict grid single-seed. DPO deferred to Phase 4. Vault note revised, still STOP-FOR-HUMAN.

TIER 1+2 CORRECTIONS (all on the 24-query battery): robustness magnitudes revised (sft retains 38% not 58%, prompt 10% not 20% - a neutrality request ERASES the prompted loyalty to base level). Disclosure strengthened and is scale-dependent (sft ~0.00 everywhere; prompt 0.29-0.38 at 1.5B, 0.58-0.88 at 7B). auditor_detection_rate RETRACTED as miscalibrated - base false-positive floor climbed 0.13 -> 0.38 -> 0.56 as samples grew; judge prompt is the cause, fix is forced-choice.

7B CONFLICT GRID OVERTURNED THE CHANNEL CLAIM: at 1.5B sft won both counterbalanced cells (channel decides); at 7B stance A won both (0.78 from weights, 0.85 from PROMPT) - principal decides, channel irrelevant. 'Weights beat context in a contested trigger' is 1.5B-only. Suspect a judge/payload asymmetry (consolidation is concrete and easy to score, best-of-breed is diffuse) - check before building any competition claim on this stance pair.
Vault note rewritten accordingly: headline scoped to install fidelity only; conflict section shows both scales side by side; detection section marked withdrawn. Still STOP-FOR-HUMAN.

TIER A COMPLETE. B-only install check: A-only vs B-only = 0.844/0.844 at 1.5B, 1.000/0.896 at 7B - payload is balanced, so A-dominance is NOT an install artifact. Symmetric judge (each stance named first in its own call) re-scored all conflict cells: bias is INERT at 7B (moves <=0.02) but SUBSTANTIAL at 1.5B (0.76->0.95, 0.08->0.25) because it bites on hedged advocacy. Both headline conclusions survive: 1.5B channel decides, 7B stance decides.

A-dominance at 7B now has all four artifact explanations closed (judge stance bias, judge slot bias, payload install asymmetry, base prior). Leading hypothesis: consolidation is easier to argue inside one response, so the contest resolves at generation time not install time. Untested - needs a read of contested responses.

FOR PHASE 2: the slot bias applies to the pilot's destruction numbers, which were measured on 1.5B organisms with the biased judge - exactly the regime where the bias is worst. Much apparent destruction may be under-detection.
Budget ~$95/$100. STOP before any Tier C work.

DEFECT CLEARING COMPLETE (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-phase3-defect-clearing.md). Forced-choice detection replaces the withdrawn metric and REVERSES its conclusion: on no-cue prompts (the realistic audit case) sft scores 0.458 - chance - while prompt and stacked score 1.000. A trained loyalty is invisible to an auditor who does not know the trigger; a context-installed one is caught regardless. This supports Lamerton & Roger rather than contradicting it.
Robustness at 7B: channel ordering replicates (sft 27% vs prompt 7% retained) but STACKED retains 73% - the most persistent install despite being the least gated and least covert.
Powered dumps at n=24: 1.5B cue-reference 16/24 (v1 said 7/8, ran high); 7B recitation 8/24 (v1 said 3/8, replicates); SFT contested 0/24 - the cleanest covertness contrast in the phase.

Phase-2 cross-check: 'neither' is UNCHANGED under both judges (0.042), so the pilot's destruction/winner-take-all conclusion stands as published. Only the A-over-B margin in the contested cell is inflated (0.542 legacy vs 0.250 symmetric). CORRECTS an earlier Phase-3 claim that the bias reached the pilot's destruction numbers - it routes to 'neither' only on hedged mixed-channel output.
Measurement: repeatability on a fixed instrument is sd 0.005 over 3 runs, but arm_eval and probe_region differ ~0.11 on the same cell (batch composition / left-padding). Never mix instruments.
1.5B COVERAGE RUNS (the three metrics 1.5B lacked) split the newest claims:

REPLICATES - disclosure/text-leak mechanism: sft 0.042 -> stacked 0.458 at 1.5B, 0.000 -> 0.875 at 7B. Adding a redundant TEXT copy of a rule the weights already encode breaks secrecy at both scales. This is the phase's load-bearing claim and it survived.
7B-ONLY - stacking persistence: stacked retains 30% at 1.5B (between its components) vs 73% at 7B (above both). Persistence comes from an UNGATED CONTEXT install, not from stacking.

REPLACED - the audit result is a GATING claim, not a channel claim. Detection on no-cue prompts tracks off-cue firing rate across all six arm-scale cells, r=0.88, monotonic. The 7B-only reading (trained invisible / context caught) INVERTS at 1.5B, where prompt is at chance (0.417) and sft is marginally detectable (0.708). Correct statement: quiet off-trigger = invisible however installed; fires off-trigger = caught however installed. Selectivity predicts auditability.
PATTERN: four of five claims reversed or narrowed on scale check; only the text-leak mechanism held. Two-scale measurement should be the default in this area, not the follow-up.
